note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Find a decumbent or ascending perennial whose complete flowering axis carries about (2–)3–7 unilateral racemes (Williamson County). On a mature raceme, paired flattened obovate spikelets can look four-ranked. Panel 2 shows TWO branches on one cut stem; panel 0 is only one cropped branch. Neither proves the total count on every plant.
tiles.short: Several one-sided racemes with paired oval spikelets
tiles.status: VISIBLE RACEMES; SAME-PLANT ROOTED HABIT GAP

tiles.heading: 02 · TRACE NODES TO THE SOIL
tiles.details: Williamson County specimens have fibrous roots and trailing shoots with adventitious roots at nodes; Kew describes lower nodal rooting as variable. Confirm actual roots on the same plant, not just stems lying along wet soil. The archived flowering head is cut, so current panels cannot verify a connected root-to-panicle specimen.
tiles.short: Perennial decumbent shoots may root at lower nodes

tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN THE INNER COLLAR
tiles.details: At the INSIDE blade–sheath junction, Williamson County describes a 1–3 mm jagged membranous ligule, with separate long hairs behind the membrane and along the collar. Panel 5 shows the actual external junction with a printed scale, NOT a spread-open measured ligule. Keep the membrane edge separate from the longer collar hairs.
tiles.short: Membranous true ligule 1–3 mm in local treatment

tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE RIPE SPIKELETS
tiles.details: At 10–20×, isolate five mature spikelets from a single verified raceme, photograph flat/convex sides and add a physical 1-mm scale. Kew reports 2.7–3.2 mm; Williamson County gives a roughly 3 × 2 mm upper glume. Panel 4 resolves real attached green oval spikelets but does not independently verify mature measurements, glume veins or pubescence.

tiles.heading: 05 · SEPARATE GLUME AND LEMMAS
tiles.details: A mature spikelet has a reduced/absent lower glume, an upper glume about spikelet-length (locally ~3 mm and three-veined), a thinner lower sterile lemma slightly shorter than the upper glume, and a hard upper fertile lemma (~2.5 mm in Williamson County; broader Kew account 2.7–3.2 mm). The sterile palea is absent locally. Glume surfaces can be GLABROUS OR minutely hairy; 'hairyseed' does not mean every mature glume must be hairy. No long true awn is present.
tiles.short: Lower glume absent; thin upper glume; firm awnless fertile lemma

tiles.heading: 06 · CHECK FLORIDA PASPALUM AND DALLISGRASS
tiles.details: Florida paspalum generally has larger ~3.5–4.2 mm broad spikelets; introduced Dallisgrass has conspicuously LONG silky upper-glume marginal hairs on mature ~3–4 mm spikelets. Thin paspalum often has smaller ~1.4–2.6 mm spikelets; panel 1 is explicitly a different-species P. setaceum comparison. Compare equally mature calibrated spikelets and actual glume hairs; do not separate pubiflorum by a cropped flowering row or by pubescence alone.
tiles.short: Size and hair origin matter more than one raceme count
tiles.status: FIELD COMPARISON; MATCHED MATURE MACROS MISSING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: PASPALUM PUBIFLORUM: a complete flowering head often has several narrow one-sided racemes, with oval flattened green spikelets. The existing Beth photograph illustrates ONLY one section of a raceme, not the whole branch count. Check several mature spikelets approximately 2.7–3.2 mm and the upper-glume fine hairs to separate from broad large-spikeleted Florida paspalum and long-silky-haired dallisgrass. NEW REAL DIAGNOSTIC PHOTO SERIES: four archived Central Texas original Harms images now show the FULL set of unilateral racemes, reproductive tissue, a close-up spikelet row and real blade/sheath junction. Source labels and rights are explicit. Compare ripe, calibrated spikelet glumes with Florida paspalum and Dallisgrass; do not claim 2.7–3.2mm from an unscaled image or identify species from one branch.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: A complete cut flowering head, actual spikelet rows and external collar-region photo are NOW archived; obtain a same-plant rooted culm, isolated mature glume with mm ruler, and OPEN inner ligule before claiming full diagnostic photo completion.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Williamson County specimens have fibrous roots and trailing shoots with adventitious roots at nodes; Kew describes lower nodal rooting as variable. Confirm actual roots on the same plant, not just stems lying along wet soil. The archived flowering head is cut, so current panels cannot verify a connected root-to-panicle specimen.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: At 10–20×, isolate five mature spikelets from a single verified raceme, photograph flat/convex sides and add a physical 1-mm scale. Kew reports 2.7–3.2 mm; Williamson County gives a roughly 3 × 2 mm upper glume. Panel 4 resolves real attached green oval spikelets but does not independently verify mature measurements, glume veins or pubescence.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: One cropped raceme never proves head branch count. A label saying 'paired' needs to show actual attachment at a node at enough resolution; the current oval row photo can't prove micro pubescence. Compare a single mature spikelet with P. floridanum and P. setaceum at 10–20×.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

intro: PASPALUM PUBIFLORUM: a complete flowering head often has several narrow one-sided racemes, with oval flattened green spikelets. The existing Beth photograph illustrates ONLY one section of a raceme, not the whole branch count. Check several mature spikelets approximately 2.7–3.2 mm and the upper-glume fine hairs to separate from broad large-spikeleted Florida paspalum and long-silky-haired dallisgrass. NEW REAL DIAGNOSTIC PHOTO SERIES: four archived Central Texas original Harms images now show the FULL set of unilateral racemes, reproductive tissue, a close-up spikelet row and real blade/sheath junction. Source labels and rights are explicit. Compare ripe, calibrated spikelet glumes with Florida paspalum and Dallisgrass; do not claim 2.7–3.2mm from an unscaled image or identify species from one branch.
memory_rule: COUNT COMPLETE RACEMES → MEASURE 5 RIPE SPIKELETS → CHECK MARGINAL HAIRS → ROOTED BASE/COLLAR. DALLIS few large silky; VASEY many small silky; FLORIDA few big round; PUBIFLORUM smaller oval; SETACEUM narrow variable; DISTICHUM two + real stolons.
safety_note: Gross photo structures are references, NOT expert confirmation. Even new licensed images are PROVISIONAL — USER PHOTO REVIEW PENDING and not proof of Hays County presence. Four Harms original images are copyrighted, permitted for scientific/educational use only WITH visible Bob Harms credit. No Creative Commons grant and no confirmed Hays voucher for each photo.
field_rule: P. pubiflorum in accepted treatments commonly has 2–5(-7) unilateral racemes, small to medium 2.7–3.2 mm spikelets with glumes glabrous or minutely pubescent. Florida paspalum usually carries larger rounder spikelets; dallisgrass has conspicuous silky marginal hairs on larger spikelets; thin paspalum's varieties can differ dramatically in foliage hairs and smaller spikelets. Without a true scale, don't force it.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
comparison_text: One cropped raceme never proves head branch count. A label saying 'paired' needs to show actual attachment at a node at enough resolution; the current oval row photo can't prove micro pubescence. Compare a single mature spikelet with P. floridanum and P. setaceum at 10–20×.
